prompt: A single red magic projectile, drawn as a flat 2D game effect sprite, flying to the left along the horizontal centre line of a wide 21:9 landscape canvas, in pure side view with no perspective. The whole shot sits in the middle of the canvas at about 60% of the canvas width, with generous empty flat green above, below and at both ends. The head leads on the left: a broad, bold, razor-sharp spearhead about one quarter as tall as it is long, built from nested jagged chevron layers of crimson #FF3658 and coral #FF7848, widest about halfway along the head, its rear edge swept back into sharp barbed sawtooth notches. The lower and rear facets are deep magenta-red #8F173C. Inside the head burns an elongated pale warm-white triangular core #FFF5DC pointing the same way, brightest at its centre. Behind the head runs a narrow, short geometric tail about as long as the head itself, made of a few thin angular crimson and magenta-red shards that taper to a thread on the right, with a handful of tiny solid square flecks in crimson and magenta-red drifting in a loose line just behind and beside it. The whole shot is drawn like a dark etched storybook engraving: every facet is separated by a fine, crisp near-black ink line #171614, about 1.5 pixels wide, as if cut with a burin, with large areas of flat colour left between the lines, and the shadow facets are hatched with fine, widely spaced near-black engraved lines and tiny stipple dots, so ink linework is visible across the whole shape while most of the area stays bright colour. The colour sits flat and matte between the ink lines, with a subtle hand-printed grain, never glossy, never a smooth gradient. The outermost edge of the shot is a slightly uneven near-black ink contour #171614, 2 pixels wide, with no coral or coloured outline outside it, and every edge drops straight onto the background, so the silhouette stays sharp and angular at tiny size. The background is one perfectly even, flat, pure chroma-key green #00FF00 filling the canvas edge to edge, smooth and evenly lit, so the shot casts no shadow on it. Every colour in the shot is near-black ink, red, coral, magenta-red or warm white; the green belongs only to the background. The canvas holds only this one shot.
